title: microLUNG Studie - Interaction between lung microbiome, allograft function, immunsystem and infections in lung transplant recipients
summary:
Despite considerable advancements in overall survival rates amongst organ transplant recipients since the introduction of immunosuppressive therapy, individuals undergoing lung transplantation (LuTx) continue to demonstrate substantially impaired long-term survival relative to recipients of other solid organ transplants. This observation persists despite the administration of lifelong immunosuppressive regimens and bronchoscopic surveillance throughout the post-transplant follow-up period.  Previous studies attributed the reduction in median survival primarily to chronic allograft dysfunction (CLAD) following LuTx and proposed a potential link to pulmonary microbiome. 
Over the past two decades, the lung microbiome- historically considered a sterile milieu solely facilitating gas exchange - has been redefined as a dynamic and complex ecosystem inhabited by a diverse range of microorganisms. 
In this context, this non-interventional observational study aims to characterize the lung microbiome of patients following LuTx. The study aims to assess the microbial richness of the lung, the distribution of individual microbiota, and their longitudinal changes throughout the post-transplant follow-up period. Furthermore, the impact of both pulmonary and gastrointestinal microbiomes on the immune system, infections and rejections should be point of investigation. Through this comprehensive analysis, the study seeks to identify risk factors associated with pulmonary infections and transplant rejections.

interventions.name: Non-interventional prospective observational study investigating the lung microbiome in lung transplant recipients at predefined time points following LuTx (intraoperative, prior extubation, 3 weeks, as well as 3, 6 and 12 months after LuTx)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- patients aged ≥ 18 years and  ≤ 67 years eligible for LuTx at LMU Klinikum Munich
- written informed consent from the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- patient's refusal to participate in the study
- patients diagnosed with HIV infection or active hepatitis
